newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: High NZ cash rate holds bill yields up at close.
newsitem.headline: High NZ cash rate holds bill yields up at close.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.95 (PREV 92.85) 90-DAYS 7.30 (PREV 7.28)
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.65 PCT (PREV 7.50) US 5-YR 6.15 (PREV 6.19)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 780.78 (PREV 765.95) Reuters NZ MCI -44 vs -59
Uncertainty over the outlook for the overnight cash rate tempered enthusiasm to buy New Zealand bank bills during Tuesday's session.
The physical bills finished two basis points higher at 7.30 percent, despite a recovery in the currency's Trade-Weighted Index to 66.31 from 66.14 at Monday's close.

The overnight cash rate bumped up to 7.65 percent, from 7.50 percent at Monday's close and as low as 6.55 percent last Thursday. One Auckland dealer said it shot as high as eight percent at one stage, prompting selling in the shorter dates. "I think if we walk in tomorrow morning and someone's trying to

push cash up to eight percent again we'll see the selling feed down through the curve into the 90-days and maybe further out as well. It's not until that happens that you'll see the futures sell," he said.

The Monetary Conditions Index NZ/MCI finished at 780.78, from 765.95 at Monday's close. In interest rate terms, conditions were 44 basis points easier than the central bank's desired level, compared to 59 easier at Monday's close.
The Reserve Bank said recently it would tolerate conditions 50 basis points either side of its assumed levels.

Dealers said they expected conditions to stay within that comfort zone until inflation data due next Tuesday, because the high overnight cash rate rendered bank bills expensive to hold and traders had lost much of their buying interest.
A surprisingly low inflation out-turn would prompt the market to re-test the RBNZ's resolve by easing conditions and waiting to see at what level the bank piped up, dealers said.
Meanwhile, mid bonds finished the day one basis point stronger at 6.71 percent, following the issue of two NZ$100 million four-year eurokiwis overnight.
The 11/06 maturity, presented with a four-basis point rally in 10-year U.S. Treasuries, managed a three pip rally of its own, to 6.88 percent.
-- Catherine McCaw, Wellington newsroom +(64 4) 471 4275
